note: PACK-002 build deterministic ZIP: two things make a ZIP non-deterministic if left alone - host enumeration order and per-entry times - and src/package/zip.zig decides both from the declaration. Entries are written in a sorted order that must already be sorted, so a caller handing host order gets a refusal rather than a differently-ordered archive; timestamps come from the declaration and default to the ZIP epoch (1980-01-01) rather than to 'now' or the file's mtime; external attributes are fixed rather than copied from the host's mode bits. Entries are stored, not deflated, on purpose: compression output can vary between library versions, and an archive whose bytes depend on which zlib is linked is not a reproducible artifact. The test builds the same declaration twice and compares bytes, and the refusals are asserted for traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, duplicates, and unsorted order. Fault proof: accepting traversal components makes the unsafe-name refusal fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
